title: Visio: Desktop MCP server lets AI clients create and edit diagrams
summary: The briefing passes: the planned capabilities and roadmap targets match the record, and searches confirmed the feature-specific documentation gaps. The Agent 365 blocking path is documented; its explanation should clarify gateway-only enforcement, and the diagram examples need an additional citation.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that the local Visio server appears in the Agent 365 registry or is covered by its blocking control.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block restricts a registered MCP server across the organisation.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: Blocking an MCP server disables all tools it exposes.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes. ... Effects on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the applicable management route. Don't assume the policy applies across all products or connected components.
claims.fix: Replace 'Blocking disables all tools the server exposes' in the note and corresponding prose with 'Blocking disables the server's tools through the applicable management route; for BYO servers, gateway blocking does not necessarily prevent direct endpoint access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-byo-mcp-server, which states 'Don't assume blocking prevents direct access to the underlying server endpoint.'
